text_fidelity_a:
Coast DX355 Double Lock Folding Knife I've been looking for a folding knife that I could use around the farm. This knife is 4.5 inches long and 1.5 inches wide when folded, so it has a nice sized blade while still being small enough not to get in my way when clipped onto my pocket. (There is a strong, nearly 3-inch-long metal clip securely screwed into the knife handle.) The entire knife appears to be made out of a sturdy, stainless steel. The handle has a texture and finger indentations to assure a secure grip when used.

I've never used a folding knife with a locking mechanism, but I expected at least some advertising pointing out how the special double-locking mechanism works. There wasn't any information included with the knife, but it was fairly easy to figure out. The linear lock is beneath the blade and automatically locks when the blade is fully extended. The safety switch is a toggle on the handle behind the blade. You can push it up when the blade is open to prevent the linear lock from being depressed (which would allow the blade to close). To close the blade, push the toggle back to the original position and depress the linear lock while folding the blade. Once I figured it out, it was easy to do.

Since it's winter, I haven't had much time to test the blade out for how well it keeps it edge or other wear issues. I'll post an update is anything significant comes up.
text_fidelity_b: Coast DX355 Double Lock Folding Knife

text_fidelity_a:
Green Guru Gear Dutchy Bike Bicycle Bike Upcycled Made in USA Pannier Bag (design may vary) I did not purchase these on Amazon, but direct from the sellers (Green Guru Gear) website. I got an EBike (Aventon Pace 500) for commuting to work and needed something to hold my personal items for a post-ride, pre-work shower. These pannier bags fill the need excellently. You can hold a lot of items in there. Everything I can fit in my gym bag, which is pretty big, I can fit in these two panniers. In addition, I can fit my full lunch bag as well. My feet do not hit the bags when I peddle. If I choose to, I could also fit my purse/backpack in them, but I carry that on my back just for more security when I ride.

I had a Topeak MTX Quick track rear rack installed on my bike to use the MTX basket with and these panniers fit perfectly on them. I can actually use the panniers and the basket at the same time because the hooks on the panniers are flush with the top of the bags and the tops of the bags are level with the top of the rack itself, so the basket can slide onto the Quick track easily with the panniers in place. So if you have even more stuff to haul on the bicycle you have all that extra space with the basket as well. Double check the weight limits on the bags and the rack before you do that though.

I knew the print on the panniers would be randomly selected when I placed my order, but I did note that they mentioned that they will try and match them if you purchase a pair, they did pretty good as both of them were in nice brown tones with pretty cool pictures/patterns on them. The bags are pretty simple to install on the rack, just hook them on and I wrap the bottom securing hook around the rack supports and hook it on sideways. The bags do not come out or off even if I go over big bumps in the road. As far as I can see about its "waterproof-ness" the material used on the cover and the front bottom half of the bags look more water "resistant", if its a few sprinkles or a light rain, it would hold up, but not a continuous downpour, especially since the sides of the bag don't appear to be water proof/resistant. The cover is secured to the front of the bag by hook & loop (Velcro) patches, they are pretty strong but cannot be locked, so if you require extra security get some type of cover to go over or secure it even more with bungee cords/nets. If you are so inclined, you could even sew on some straps with securing clips on them.

If I don't use the basket with the bags, they are easy to remove and carry. Carry by the short handles or the adjustable and convenient shoulder straps as well. They fold up for easy, low profile storage when not in use, either on the bike rack or somewhere else. I would not leave these unattended on a bicycle, they are so nice that someone may be tempted to steal them (probably those same crumbs that take the bicycle lights if you don't take them with you). If I use the basket also, it will have to be removed before removing the bags.

Overall, I am happy with my purchase of the Green Guru Dutchy pannier bags, I would recommend them for anyone considering getting panniers for your bicycle rack(s). They are great looking on the bicycle and pretty unique from other panniers.
text_fidelity_b: Green Guru Gear Dutchy Bike Bicycle Bike Upcycled Made in USA Pannier Bag (design may vary)

Topeak Mini Morph Bike Pump , Silver, Black, 26 x 5 x 2.8 cm / 10.2” x 2.0” x 1.1” I've had similar push down frame pump I bought at Performance bicycle(their house brand) for over ten years and it saved me from miles of walking countless times. Only problem I had with it was it goes only to about 65 PSI(I normally inflate them to 100), so I had to come home very slowly to avoid pinch flat.
I just received Topeak pump today and first thing I tried was if I can push it over 100 PSI. It does, but not without some effort but it depends on your strength not by the limitation of the pump.
This pump is shorter and lighter than my old pump and I can secure it on my back pack I've been using it for my old pump without any modification.
The dimension I measured was 262mm long. The weight is 151g(The spec says 170g but I think that includes the bracket.).
Some caution: the chuck is pretty tight fit, if you are not careful when you pull it out, the stem may come off with it(like I did). I replaced it with new tube and tried it again and it seems that the chuck doesn't need to be so deep on the valve.
The over all quality seems to be very good. The materials and the fit of the parts are solid. In my opinion, it's well worth the price I paid.
Recommended.

I wish I could post some photos but the new layout doesn't seem to allow me to do that. If someone know how to post a photo, please let me know.

The Friendly Swede Survival Pod - 20 Accessories Emergency Paracord (Black) I received this as a free review sample. For some reason I am drawn to survival kits such as this. The two most useful tools (to me) are the fire starter and the saw. However, in a true survival situation everything in the kit will probably prove useful, and some may even make a big difference.

Also useful is the paracord itself. It is not designed for climbing and supporting your weight, but will definitely allow you to lash together a shelter. Ironically, the implements are inside the paracord pouch, so the ziplock style bag becomes storage for as many of those as you can cram. Frankly, I think that the cardboard box that this comes in should be retained for better storage (albeit not very waterproof.)

* Long - the length is longer than most of his other jackets so protects him more against the rain.

* Navy color - won't show soil easily, and goes with all colors of pants.

There is a slight scent from the fabric which should dissipate as it airs out. It smells like nylon.

My husband was thrilled with this jacket when he put it on. We've had a LOT of rain in the northeast this spring and summer - 4-5 days a week! - so this jacket will come in handy.

text_fidelity_a:
Cutters Gamer Padded Receiver Football Gloves, EXTRA GRIP, Youth & Adult sizes I selected these gloves knowing they would be a little small for me but thinking they would fit my teenage son better. As it turns out the size runs small and you really need to buy up one or two sizes to get them to fit just right.

These are athletic gloves and are well-suited for racquet sports, football, basketball, golf and other ball sports as well as biking. They will also work for weight lifting though I would not recommend these for that purpose but instead would recommend something a bit more ruggedized. The palm and print-side fingers are made of a vinyl-like material that is not sticky but slightly tacky and makes gripping and holding very easy. The rest of the gloves are made of light, stretchy material and leatherette material which breathes really well. There is a Velcro wrist strap which tightens the grip around the wrist and keeps the gloves in place.

There are padded sections across the knuckles and on the fingers and thumb which are great for reducing impact damage and pain if you bang your hands (playing racquetball is one situation in which this can happen). This is something I have not seen on work gloves but would appreciate.

These seem to be made very well. I have found no loose threads, uneven seams or imperfections in the materials that would give me any pause with these gloves. I have no issues with the materials and workmanship.

I received a pair of Adult Large gloves. I have hands like a gorilla so I knew they would not fit me very well at all. However, my son is smaller (5’5”, proportional and athletic build) and I figured they would work well for him. I asked him to put them on and try them out, and he complained that they were a bit small even for him, particularly when the Velcro strap was pulled tight. So, for him, an XL is the right size and for me XXL would be right. This is the only issue with these gloves we have found – large should have been appropriate for him, but instead they almost fit.

These are very nice gloves and they are very well made. Just remember to buy a size or two larger than you think you need.
text_fidelity_b: Cutters Gamer Padded Receiver Football Gloves, EXTRA GRIP, Youth & Adult sizes

text_fidelity_a:
Lonely Planet Korea I have lots of guidebooks - and lots of Lonely Planets, for that matter. But despite the fact that they say they are for "independent travellers", I keep finding ridiculous reviews on restaurants and hotels, to the point where I've stopped using them.

The History, Snapshot, and similar sections are great, but if you have a brain of your own - use it. Forget their restaurant and hotel recommendations, as I'm not even sure they visit the places. Sometimes they have history or comments on places that is worthwhile to read, though. All tourbooks may have these drawbacks, to be fair.

Finally, I think I'm going to stop buying Lonely Planet's, though. First, they always act like driving is so scary everywhere, when it's actually quite easy to anyone with a brain. They also forget to give worthwhile tips on getting a car, etc. I imagine that this is their way of "saving the Earth". To a person who does care about the Earth, but doesn't believe that being a dirty hippie is going to save anything, this - and all their other BS trying to coerce their opinions onto you as fact - gets really freakin' old. Yes, yes, I know, LP is founded by some hippie freak from AUS or something - whooptie doo. That doesn't mean I have to pay some jerk who's going to push his politics on me, whether I agree with them or not.
text_fidelity_b: Lonely Planet Korea

JACO MBX-60 Presta Tire Pressure Gauge for Bikes (Max 60 PSI) | MTB & XC Series The old saying that a person who has one watch always knows what time it is, but a person who has two watches is never sure, comes to mind here. If this is your only pressure gauge and you dial in your tire pressures based on this tool, you’ll be happy. But if you have a couple of different gauges like me, some on pumps and another that is independent like this one, then you won’t be exactly sure which one is accurate.

However, consistency and precision is what matters. Based on several years of use and comparison to two other gauges and my car readouts, I trust my digital gauge on my bike floor pump for accuracy from psi ranges in the mid teens to the mid 50s. I took readings from several different pressures as benchmarked with my pump, and this analog gauge consistently read about 1 psi lower. That consistency is more than good enough for me. And by way of background, I’ve set up my mountain bike and gravel bike with tubeless tires, and I am particular about the pressures I run in different conditions.

Also, this gauge has a rubberized face and comes in a sturdy and well padded case. Since this is a precision instrument, I appreciate the protection to keep this device working well.

Overall this is an easy to use tool that feels like it will last a long time (as long as you don’t abuse it).

My quads are pretty tight, and when foam rolling with the trigger point roller, it was like a deep tissue massage; the vibration makes a significant difference in the give of the muscles, in that it allows the roller to go deeper for the same amount of pain from a conventional roller. I also felt a huge relief when rolling my glutes: its small size allows it to get into those hard-to-reach muscles.

The trigger point roller doesn't have any give when putting your weight on it like other rollers, but the vibration helps counteract the stiffness of the product.

The only thing I encountered is that the button sometimes doesn't respond, and I have to keep pressing it until it works.

I give this little device five stars. Maybe the next one can be heated?…

text_fidelity_a:
Omron HJ-112 Digital Pocket Pedometer This is the 2nd pedometer I've owned. I bought this Omron to replace Walk 4 Life (W4L) unit I used for the prior 7 months. I was happy with the W4L pedometer except that the clip broke twice on it. And, because the clip is part of the basic W4L housing, you can't just purchase another clip - the unit is basically ruined (unless you want to risk carrying it loose in your pocket and opening it with your thumbnail). Therefore, since this Omron pedometer fits inside a separate hard plastic clip housing, I decided to try it.

It functions well, accurately tracks your steps, and has a nice memory feature to review the past week. However, it is close to 3 times the size of the W4L and, therefore, too bulky to wear under nice clothes. I was able to clip the W4L to my bra under a relatively tight fitting top, and it was undetectable; the Omron looks like a growth is projecting out of your chest. This seems to defeat the purpose of tracking all your steps if you can't (or choose not to) wear it, let's say, on a night you go dancing. In addition, although there's much less chance of the clip breaking, it's uncomfortable against bare skin and seems to me to be much bulkier than necessary.

In spite of these design flaws, it's a nice little unit for wearing around the house or in a casual/workout environment. In general, I've found pedometers to be a fantastic way to motivate individuals to just stay active, which is much more effective than exercise alone. If the only way pedometer manufacturers can prevent the clips from breaking is to make them as Omron has, it's far better than W4L's clip design.

If Omron could reduce the size of the unit, the bulkiness of the clip, and have the unit sit low in the clip housing (instead of half of it sticking up over the top), I'd give it 5 stars.
text_fidelity_b: Omron HJ-112 Digital Pocket Pedometer

text_fidelity_a:
Lifestyle by Focus Electric Travel Cooler/Warmer Portable Camping Cooler Hard Cooler Ice Chest Roller Wheeled Cooler for Car, Home, Beach, Fishing, Camping, Party (Blue) Large 48 Quart, Holds 60 cans So far, I am underwhelmed. I purchased this in advance of a cross-country trip and an extended stay in a budget hotel that doesn't have a room fridge - hence the choice of dual power source. Being the prudent sort, I plugged it in at home to see whether it really would cool down to 40 degrees. House was 75 degrees, cooler after running all night was 55 degrees, at best. I'll probably keep it, and maybe as a beer or cola cooler it's fine, but as for being able to keep perishables such as eggs, milk, lunch meat and cheese in the hotel, or in transit for 1000 miles, for that matter, I'm not sure it's worth the risk of food poisoning to rely on its cooling capability. It's also smaller inside than I was expecting.

Update: On a second, and much longer, trip, I took this along, mostly for refrigeration in transit, but then when I reached my destination, I found that the full-size fridge was on the blink, so I plugged this in and it kept stuff reasonably cold, including the return trip, although still not much lower than 40-degrees. All told, some of the stuff I carried with me was still good when I got back home eleven days later, and maybe some of that was due to having also packed big bottles of frozen drinking water (ice) and starting out with other frozen foods; maybe some of it was due to my travel being in weather that was at freezing or below and the cooler rode for part of the trip in an unheated truck boot. All that being said, I still wouldn't be totally reliant on it in the summer, and would still pack the bottled ice - which is also a good way to gauge just how well the cooler is doing its job.
text_fidelity_b: Lifestyle by Focus Electric Travel Cooler/Warmer Portable Camping Cooler Hard Cooler Ice Chest Roller Wheeled Cooler for Car, Home, Beach, Fishing, Camping, Party (Blue) Large 48 Quart, Holds 60 cans

text_fidelity_a:
ETROL Mini First Aid Kit - Upgrade 117 Piece Personal Compact Emergency Survival Kits,Lightweight Portable Essential Medical Supplies for Car Backpacking Camping Home Travel Boat The information provided in the written part of the product description needs to line up with the pictures as well as what is actually sent. It is NOT THE SAME as what you read or see. There are some spots that are the same, and many that are different. I CAN NOT RECOMMEND THIS based on the mixed information.

HERE IS WHAT I RECEIVED:
--A smooth, zippered soft "hard shell" case (firm but flexible. Think of a cheap sunglass case). This is not at all what is pictured NOR described in the product information. What is pictured is a totally different material. It may not make a difference if you are just looking for some supplies, OR it may make all the difference if you are looking for a particular container as well as supplies. With this as the description, "Durable & Portable Tactical Molle Pouch】ETROL mini Survival Gear is ultralight, compact and portable with a Velcro strap system compatible with MOLLE so that it can be hooked to the backpack, belt or other. It offers large compartments and plenty of room to add your own equipment, including a special phone pocket and an emergency pen slot" NOPE NOPE NONE OF THIS. Just a smooth zippered shell. No means to use it as part of MOLLE system, no extra compartments or special pockets or place to have a pen. They are describing a product even different than shown, and even further off from what I received.

--The product description also states (as of 3/31/20) that, "【Quick Access & Top Quality Durable Supplies】The Survival Gear Kit includes the most popular outdoor survival necessities: 3-mode Tactical Flashlight, black stainless steel Tactical Military Knife, Fire Starter, Compass of the military class, a Multi-Function Tool Card, a loudly Whistle with 120db, Emergency Blankets which can retain 90% of body heat and more. Being customized and uniquely tested, our Survival First Aid Kit is designed to prepare you well in case of outdoor activities " NOPE!! Plastic whistle and emergency blanket, yes. Flashlight, military knife, fire starter, compass, Multi function tool card.. NOPE. I actually didn't expect this, but for it to state this in the description? False advertisement!

Kit is described as measuring 7.5" x 5.1" x 2"
MY KIT measures roughly, 6.5" x 4.75" x 2.5"

--The product description DOES seem to accurately state the medical supplies portion, "【FDA Approved & Professional Treatment Supplies】This First Aid Kit contains the most important first aid supplies for various treatments on the market. Buckle Tourniquet, PBT conforming bandage, Tourniquet, non-woven tape, first aid scissors, plastic tweezers, sterile gauze, a lot of alcohol swabs, cotton swabs, PE adhesive bandages, and safety pins, to stop massive bleeding, dressing or disinfection of wounds nd more, which will come in handy in case of unforeseen events". To see what you are getting, I can say that it 100% matches up to the product description PICTURE of the supplies. ((NOT THE CASE, though))

Furthermore,
--The kit I have has a fairly useless first aid manual. It is labeled as being by "Firstar" (as are the medical packaging), and is visually messy as well as minimally informative. Consider it non essential and add your own emergency steps. As for the contents, again, it is as described according to the product description and pictures. YET If compared to the information provided on the manual, it would not come close to being the same items. For what it is worth, what comes in this kit according to the product description picture is much better.

--Other plusses include that I am pleased with all that is in there, how well it is packed, how easy it is to access the items as well as how surprisingly easy it was to get everything back into the container.

--However I take issue with the misinformation between what is described and what I received. Even if they totally took out the part on all the tactical goodies that is supposed to be in it, and just focused on the medical.. then there would still be the problem of the TOTALLY DIFFERENT case than what is pictured and described. The soft/hard shell zippered case is OK enough, and would be FINE if it were pictured and described as such. But if you are expecting a MOLLE bag/attach capable (that's a big thing), then this would be hugely disappointing.

--So overall, I can not in good conscience recommend a product when it is so far off from what is pictured and described. I have no idea what it costs, and you better believe that a MOLLE style/attachment capable bag is worth more than this soft/hard shell.

--I would include pictures but the photo/video uploader that Amazon usually has in the reviews has been missing for about a week now. If I see that it comes back up, I will be sure to show you the case I have, then you can see how different it is. Again, case is a firm smooth soft shell with zipper. Bright red and labeled, "first aid kit"

If the product description (plus pic of the container) changes, then I can edit this as is reasonable.

Again-- the actual contents according to the picture/graphic is correct. The case is not. The description of the case and other items is entirely wrong. The list of items this kit contains according to the useless weird manual is also wrong, BUT the items included here are better. SO do with this information as you will. I hope it helped you today. Despite the errors in information, it is possible that what I described happens to be exactly what you are looking for. My 1 star rating could be your 5 :)
text_fidelity_b: ETROL Mini First Aid Kit - Upgrade 117 Piece Personal Compact Emergency Survival Kits,Lightweight Portable Essential Medical Supplies for Car Backpacking Camping Home Travel Boat

text_fidelity_a:
Thule Upslope Snowsports Backpack, 35 L This pack was designed for back-country skiing. For a detailed look at the design and features of the book I highly recommend checking out Thule's video in the listing. It's very well shot, quickly gets to the point, and gives a complete overview of the features. That being said, here's my review on this versatile piece of travel gear.

I ride longboard skateboards, and the snowboard attachment is perfect for holding a decent sized deck. Even if you don't have a use for the ski or snowboard attachments they tuck neatly away and the bag still has perfect functionality for travel or hiking. It's light, durable and has strong seams and zippers. There are multiple compartments for ease of access for different types of items, though the largest compartment opens from behind the straps and the bag must be removed before you can access it.

One of the most clever features is a well engineered elastic interior. The bag is very compressed but expands with the load that you place in the main compartment. It can expand to 35 liters, which is quite impressive, but it also will hold much less than that securely without sagging or getting off balance. That is what makes this bag for me - it's versatile whether you're traveling for either a weekend or a full week.

Provided that you load the bag securely according to Thule's recommendations, this bag is very comfortable when strapped on your back. A chest and waist strap are included to share the load, and they work very well to disperse the weight evenly. The shoulder straps fit high and feel very secure when adjusted properly, and they don't pull at your back like many other packs can.

All of the pockets, seams, zippers and hardware are top quality and appear to be made to last. I'll be heading on a trip to Europe soon and will be taking this as my carry-on (it won't fit fully loaded under a seat but will fit in an overhead fine). I have a feeling this bag is going to be first in my list of travel gear for a long time. I definitely recommend picking one up.
text_fidelity_b: Thule Upslope Snowsports Backpack, 35 L

text_fidelity_a:
Coleman ComfortSmart Suspension Camping Chair After a month-long search for a balcony chair while visiting too many different stores, I finally found this one at BJ's for $39.99. It is a dream to sit in because the material has a lot of give which makes it very comfortable. What I also like is:

- it has a high back and a slight recline to it
- there's a small cup holder (more for a soda can than anything else) that easily folds out from under the right side of the seat
- it appears to be built very sturdy
- it opens with ease
- the arm rests are comfortable and covered in foam
- the chair comes in a nice carrying bag
- the back (which looks white in the picture on Amazon) is actually clear mesh; like a pair of black pantyhose but very strong.

The only negatives are that the chair is heavy, very tall and has a large footprint. Originally, I purchased two of these but because of the large footprint was only able to fit one comfortably on the available space on my balcony. The fact that I kept only one of these chairs when I wanted to keep two speaks volumes since I only buy chairs in pairs. However, this is the most comfortable lawn/balcony/beach chair I ever sat in in my life so forget about any potential visitor he or she can stand on the balcony during a visit instead.

By the way, I must have tried over 30 beach and other folding chairs before I found this one. In fact, I purchased a total of 3 different chairs (in sets of 2) in a state of desperation and took all of them back except for this one. The two Lifetime Comfort folding chairs I purchased at BJs for $19.99 were exceptionally sturdy but too clinical looking even though they were relatively comfortable for a straight-backed chair. After returning those, I purchased 2 Picnic Time Portable Folding Sports Chairs in Hunter Green for $39.99 each at TJ Maxx. I almost kept those but when I saw these I bought 2 at BJs for $39.99 each and compared them to the comfort of the Picnic Time chairs. The Coleman won by a long shot. If I had the room, I would have kept the second suspension chair as a backup. I hope this chair lasts a long, long time and is actually as sturdy as it feels.

This was a great buy!
text_fidelity_b: Coleman ComfortSmart Suspension Camping Chair

text_fidelity_a:
SHIMANO UN55 BB Square Taper Bottom Bracket I only have one ride in with this BB so far, but already I can tell it's a night-and-day improvement over the vintage BB it replaces.

I tooled up to overhaul the old BB on a ca. 1990 Trek, and that went well except for the condition of the spindle; it had already become pitted from foreign objects grinding around in there.

The new UN55 is butter smooth and feels more solid, too.

My only reservation is the spacing. I measured slightly under 113mm on the old spindle, so figured the 113mm UN55 would be the tiniest bit wide. In fact it was a tiny bit narrow, as the chainrings lined up slightly to the left of where they were. I adjusted the limit screw and tension on the front derailleur and the bike seems to work fine now. Not sure whether I should try a wider BB or what; I'm new to proper road bike mechanics. Also I didn't actually measure the new spindle to verify that it really is 113mm; I only noticed the discrepancy after I assembled the whole thing and I didn't want to back out all the parts just to measure....

My UN55 was shipped from Bell's Bike Shop and it was missing the bolts. I had to go to a local store and get a couple of spare bolts from their parts bin.
text_fidelity_b: SHIMANO UN55 BB Square Taper Bottom Bracket

text_fidelity_a:
Jetboil MightyMo Ultralight and Compact Camping and Backpacking Stove This little camping system works great! Living in California, I've had a series of planned power outages and I had previously and had zero experience cooking with a camp stove. However, once I got over my trepidation, and purchased the branded accessories that go with this kit, I found that this was a very simple cooking solution to use outside during these outages, and it's very lightweight and tiny to store.

I initially purchased a pot support and the jet boil pot, only to find out that I did not actually need the pot support with this model. This is clear on the product page now, but at the time it was not made clear. The jet boil pot did an amazing job of boiling water and cooking things with a high liquid content. It does create a significant hotspot so I found it less good for cooking thicker soups or things like tasty bite lentils. With those things, even with the flame turned down almost as far as it would go, I still got some things sticking to the (I believe anodized aluminum) surface.

I also purchased the nonstick skillet from the brand, because I wanted to be sure that whatever I got was going to work with my stove and be the right size not to tip things over. The skillet also gets some significant hotspots, but by my second morning of cooking eggs, I was doing a much better job of making toast on the skillet and then making eggs to go with and not getting too many brown spots on the eggs.

I purchased my fuel from the hardware store, where it was a much better price than purchasing it online. You do not need to use the branded fuel they sell, which is good because the branded fuel is extremely expensive, as is any fuel when purchased online given the shipping considerations and restrictions.

In terms of setting up this unit, there is a support that holds the gas canister and makes the whole unit much more sturdy, yet the support itself pulls off of the canister and folds down into a tiny little triangle that goes in the palm of your hand. The actual stove also fits in the palm of your hand when all of the pieces are folded down and is this tiny little thing that does not look like it would support a whole cooking pot, but it does. When everything is unfolded perfectly, things do sit steadily on the unit. I found it very easy to twist the unit onto the gas canister, use the little twister to turn the fuel on, and then click the igniter to ignite the fuel and make a fire. Then it was a simple matter from their to cook my food, then turn the little twister again to turn off the fuel entirely. I did store the unit on the gas canister during the duration of the power outage, but disconnected it for storage.

Even as a rookie user of such things, I found it fairly easy to get the hang of doing some good cooking on this thing and after the first power outage had tailored my food supply to things that this unit would cook well – either things that can be fried with the nonstick skillet, or things with a very high liquid content or that you add boiling water too.

Overall I was really pleased with the whole array of accessories that go with this unit and I really appreciate the flux ring cooking pot in particular, which got my boiling water ready for tea in about two minutes. This was very much appreciated in the rain, when I was huddling under the eaves trying not to get wet while making my morning caffeine.
text_fidelity_b: Jetboil MightyMo Ultralight and Compact Camping and Backpacking Stove

text_fidelity_a:
Sabre Tactical Pepper Gel with Belt Holster for Easy Carry, Maximum Police Strength OC Spray, Quick Access Flip Top Safety, Tactical Design for Security Professionals, 18 Bursts, 18-Foot Range Every method of self-defense involves a level of awareness and confidence. Exercising "situational awareness" will often allow you to avoid placing yourself in a position where you have to protect yourself. Escape of course is the second option assuming that there is an effective way to avoid a confrontation. But if you are finally forced to bring your use of force to the situation, you must be confident of your method and how to effectively deploy it.

Many years ago I tested a Sabre product for effectiveness. Having a wife and two young daughters motivated me to find something legal that they could carry and use properly without hurting themselves in the process. The particular Sabre unit I tested DID NOT PERFORM AS ADVERTISED! I wrote a poor product review and explained why I came to that conclusion. Unfortunately my review was targeted by numerous individuals who trashed my reasoning and perspective. Yes, the Sabre products have an outstanding reputation. But not every individual unit will work as promised!

About 35 years ago I worked as a product development manager for a company lastly known as We Care America -- formerly Weapons Corporation of America (WCA). One of the products we brought to market was a pepper spray intended for self-defense use. I couldn't put my name on the recommendation until I satisfied myself as to its effectiveness. That meant that I had to be sprayed in the face. Many law enforcement organizations require their officers to be sprayed so that they understand the proper use and deployment of their spray -- and so they know what their targeted individuals will go through.

My suggestion to you is to take your unit outside the house, find an area that is not windy, hold your off-hand away from you with the palm down, and spray the back of your hand a quick burst. You should feel sharp pain on the back of your hand. If you don't, you have a defective unit. If you do, simply wash off with soap and warm water. DO NOT PUT YOUR HANDS NEAR YOUR EYES!

A unit failure can be caused by a short expiration date, poor storage, or less than optimal shipping conditions. Even on this product page Sabre states that other brands experience a 30% failure rate (University of Utah study). If your unit produces the desired irritation, shoot a full burst away from you to get an idea of how well your can is pressurized. Your spray may not go the promised 18 feet. Be aware of its particular limitations. In any event, return it immediately if it doesn't perform as advertised.

Once you determine that your individual unit is effective, make sure to view the offered free training video and then practice deploying your unit without actually spraying it. You must have confidence in both your individual unit and in yourself. Practice may seem redundant but it can be a life saver.
text_fidelity_b: Sabre Tactical Pepper Gel with Belt Holster for Easy Carry, Maximum Police Strength OC Spray, Quick Access Flip Top Safety, Tactical Design for Security Professionals, 18 Bursts, 18-Foot Range

text_fidelity_a:
Prorack Kayak Carrier My only previous experience carrying kayaks has been tying them to the top of a rental car with old patch cords through the windows. So my comments here might not be wise, but hopefully a fresh perspective.

First thing I noticed is that you have to have the cross bars installed on your roof rack, not just the bars that run perpendicular to your windshield.

I really like the idea and design on the four "pads" that you lock down, they flex in (or out) to conform somewhat to the bottom of your vessel. They give you confidence that the pressure you apply is working with you and not against you (not that you're applying too much).

They lock on fairly easily with a simple bolt and sort of a wing-nut type add-on. This could be slightly better. You have to pull that wing-nut add-on back to encase the head of the bolt, which is intuitive and not difficult, but the system reminds me of a tool for cutting lock holes in doors that I broke the first day. An all metal specialty-bolt would inspire much more confidence.

The straps they give you are just okay. They work, but they're not the heavy duty ratcheting straps you might be imagining. Similarly the ropes and hooks they give you to tie down the front and the back are less impressive than some specialty-cut bungee cords with rubber-covered hooks on one end and quick attachment mechanism on the other that you might wish for.

I don't have a high opinion of the general public, and thus I remove all such equipment from my car, even when it is possible to lock it in place. Locks are always appreciated, though, although half the time they are just "best effort" on these types of devices anyway. Even so, they're fairly quick to remove and replace, especially if you can mark or remember the exact placement.

In summary, this is a good (and apparently unique, from reading other reviews) idea, and the bulk of the product seems to be of high quality. A few bucks extra spent on higher quality accessories would kick this up to a premium product.
text_fidelity_b: Prorack Kayak Carrier

text_fidelity_a:
Plano Stowaway Micro Organizer Premium Tackle Organization I don't know why everybody is having problems with these 3214 boxes. I've been using them for years - at least 10 years - the brownish kind that's labeled "Micro Mag". I've never had a single problem with them and I prefer them over the 3414 soft plastic white ones, although these are slightly heavier than the 3414's. When I want to just carry one little kit in my vest or pocket, these are perfect. I've accidentally dropped them on hard surfaces without any breakage or cracks. Of course, I'm sure there's a limit to how much abuse they will take, but if you're careful with your fishing gear there should be no problem.

Since I gave two of them away to my son and wife, I needed a replacement. I tried to consolidate all of my trout gear into one, but found I could be a little more organized with two. I use one for all my terminal tackle, hooks and weights (separated by size) and I'll use the other one for all my lures. The problem I have with the white 3414 box is that the lids don't seal tightly. Every one I've ever had or inspected on the shelf has the same issue. The lids are slightly bowed out. So, when you put a bunch of tiny #14 hooks, swivels, and the like, they always end up migrating to another section. Really irritating. That NEVER happens with the hard 3214.

When I saw these green ones (I've never seen them in the stores), I thought it was perfect. I like the color and it differentiates between my brown one. Comparing it to my old brown one, it is exactly the same - except mine is not labeled Micro Mag like in the picture. The top is just kind of plain with a small Plano logo. I actually prefer this because it makes seeing the contents easier.

As far as all the complaints with the latches not catching, I have NO idea what that's all about. I've handled dozens of these things and never seen that problem, nor have I ever gotten one that didn't work perfectly. You'd have to have pretty poor quality control to let so many go out into the market as seem to be reported, and I personally think Plano has pretty good QC.
text_fidelity_b: Plano Stowaway Micro Organizer Premium Tackle Organization

text_fidelity_a:
H2OSUP Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board 10'6''/10' × 30" × 6" with Premium SUP Paddle Board Accessories & Backpack, Ultra-Light, Wide Stable Design, Non-Slip Deck for Youth & Adults My wife and I have wanted to get on the water with SUPs or kayaks since trying them on a tour a few years ago, however, unable to have any storage at home, we have been unable to. Then we saw inflatable SUPs and thought we’d be able to give that a try. I had the opportunity to get this H2OSUP Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board and I jumped! Of course, we live in a hot weather state with summer rainy (storm) season and I’ve had major surgery this year with a longer recovery, so unfortunately we have not yet been able to get onto the water. But as the weather calms and I’ve been cleared... we’ll be out there sooner than later. In the mean time, we finally had a chance to blow up this H2OSUP Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board and so far so good - we are sure this is going to turn out to be a great thing for us! This H2OSUP Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board comes with several items to get you going (able cuff, repair kit, pump), but do not forget, you’ll want to have some sort of safety vest (required by law in our state - NOT INCLUDED in this kit).

The pump to get it inflated is included and for us, worked pretty well. We took turns to pump it up and while it took some time (and strength we’re both currently lacking post surgery and injury) we were still able to get it “almost fully inflated.” I say “almost” because the company recommended 15 PSI and we only got to 10. That 15 is for “optimal use” and no higher. We felt like the 10 would be good, but when we are out there (and I have more energy back) we will go a bit higher than the 10 As you can see in the pics, it is very inflated and looks good, my wife able too and on it and feel firm and secure. Standing on it she said it felt like (on water) it’ll have good, solid balance and allow a feeling of security on the water. This SUP looks and feels “narrow and long” to us based on our experiences on tours, but something we both would feel comfortable on. We will update this review once we can get out there. In the mean time, we are really happy with this SUP and how easily it went together. Or blown into shape. The removal of air was easy and took only a couple minutes. I’ll say, when she first opened the valve there was a LOUD HIGH PITCHED!!! sound that hurt both our ears, but it went away pretty quickly. Then completed the air removal. My wife did point out the ONE CON is this H2OSUP Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board has a VERY pointy and painful value piece you push on - it was not at all comfortable and hurt her finger enough she grabbed a piece of the wrapping it came in to cushion her finger.

We have not used nor opened the paddle that came with. We felt like its weight in the bag was alright, but had a chance to get another that was lighter. We will try both. But we also feel like having two paddles is safest - one with in case something happens to the second.

There are hooks on the deck where you can attach a kayak seat for sitting down - something I prefer. I have weaker ankles from years of sports, so I can tire easily on SUPs. I’ll look forward to this addition - NOT INCLUDED in this kit, but available from H2O as an add-on.

Overall this H2OSUP Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board is a great board and we are even more excited to get to our coast and use it. In the mean time, we are very happy with how easy this SUP gets set up and takes down and feel like it’s sturdy and well made enough it’ll be great for a good long time.
text_fidelity_b: H2OSUP Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board 10'6''/10' × 30" × 6" with Premium SUP Paddle Board Accessories & Backpack, Ultra-Light, Wide Stable Design, Non-Slip Deck for Youth & Adults

text_fidelity_a: Franklin Sports Mini Putt Golf Game for Kids - Spin n' Putt Electronic Putting Game - Indoor Mini Golf for Kids + Toddlers - Putter + Balls Included The Franklin spin n putt golf game is a pretty cool game. There are 10 holes/slots for the golf balls to land in with points ranging from 5 to 100. 5 of the 10 balls are white and the other 5 are yellow. Once you decide who goes first he or she will putt all 5 balls toward the base. Anything not in a slot counts as 0 points. After player one shoots player 2 gets to shoot his or her 5 balls. Clearly, you are able to make up your own game and rules.  The one thing I like about this set is that there is no putting green strip. Therefore you are able to putt from any angle or even try to bounce off a wall and into the slots. Accu-Gage by Milton Shrader Valve Bike Tire Pressure Gauge with Bleed Valve, for 0-160 PSI - ANSI Certified This is labled as a bicycle tire pressure guage on the box, but I bought it as an inexpensive alternative to measure lower level pressures on nitrogen gas charged shock absorbers. Of course it's also suitable for tire pressures but the scale is a bit high for the typical pressures I run (15 to 55 psi perhaps). On gas-charged shocks pressures range from 125 to 300psi. The proper guages or regulators are expensive. Fortunately the pressure levels I wanted to measure were on the lower-end. They turned out to be 135 psi. In fact I merely wanted to verify they met minimum requirements. With this guage I was able to do that for about a tenth the cost of a 300 psi regulator that is typically used for the purpose. It's also quite handy to keep for measuring tire pressures since my 90psi guage was broken (you can guess how).

In summary, this is a nice little guage with a brass fitting for a very reasonable cost.
text_fidelity_b: Accu-Gage by Milton Shrader Valve Bike Tire Pressure Gauge with Bleed Valve, for 0-160 PSI - ANSI Certified

text_fidelity_a: CamelBak Eddy Kids Vacuum Insulated Stainless Steel Bottle 12 oz,  Stainless My husband and I have used Camelbak bottles for over 15 years, and we both still use our insulated stainless bottles that are 9 years old. Our kids have been using the camelbak kids bottles for the past 2 years, and while I don’t believe a perfect kids water bottle exists, these are my favorite option. The main problem I’ve seen with camelbak kids bottles is that my 2 and 3 year old chew on the bite valve, which cause it to split wider than it should, then drip when the valve is open and it’s laying on its side. I have probably purchased 8 replacement bite valves for their bottles in the past 2 years because they only seem to last us 6 months or so before the leaking gets out of control. Thankfully Amazon sells 4 packs of replacement valves. If your kid is older and doesn’t chew on it as much, or even if they shut the valve after taking a drink, then that shouldn’t be an issue. Overall I like the camelbak design and I can clean it really well using a bottle brush and straw cleaner. As far as this stainless option goes, it is obviously more prone to being dented and banged up. We already have a nice gouge in the side after being dropped from 2 feet on to tile. But it will keep drinks cold for pretty much the whole day if you give it a few cubes of ice, and there won’t be condensation on the bottle. I love that I can put ice in this and not worry about it making a condensation puddle on my coffee table! I will happily take the dents in exchange for cold water all day long.

If you are mounting on a standard stud/sheetrock wall, BE SURE TO SCREW THE HANGER BRACKET INTO A WALL STUD. The manufacturer recommends installing only on a masonry wall, but if you attach to a wall stud, it will be fine. Sawyer Products SP2129 Micro Squeeze Water Filtration System, 1 Pack, Black/Blue One thing you don't want to scrimp on is water filtering when you're hiking. Sawyer has an excellent reputation in the field, and we've used a different Sawyer filter for two years quite happily. This is a nice addition to their line-up.

Pros:
Size: it's small, compact, and quite light

Easy to use: screw it on to the included 32 0z. bladder once you've filled it, onto most regular types of disposable plastic water bottles (but please don't use those!), onto many bladders, or use the included straw to drink from the water source directly (though less comfortably). That's it.

Water flow: It comes out quickly enough to drink directly without any annoying pause or lag (you can also squeeze the bag for more flow).

Drinking bag feels quite durable, always a concern for these sorts of filters. I wouldn't be worried about this one.

Comes with an extra gasket, straw, and cleaning syringe

Backflushing is easy and quick

Quasi-negatives
Doesn't do viruses. I don't consider this a real negative since a) if you're hiking in the US you don't need to worry about viruses and b) if you're looking for something to take care of viruses you're looking for a real step up in price and product so that's a whole different category

No instructions. This is more just a little annoying, but easily solved by going online and looking at the videos.

It's a great little product from a trustworthy source. Water filters have come a long way from the old bulky pump action and so if you're still using one of those, consider moving up to something like this. So much easier and better to carry.

text_fidelity_a:
Jaybird Reign Advanced Active Fitness Recovery Band - Black - S/M I bought this from Amazon based on all the 5 star reviews. I have been wearing it consistently for 11 days and following the instructions as noted in the on-line user guide videos. I am torn as to whether to give this 3 or 4 start. I ended up going with 4 stars because I have tried other trackers and the REIGN feature-set is hands above the other devices I have tried. For me it is the best choice available, today.

PROS
SIZING: Band design and fit is excellent. You are given 3 band lengths with every device, which ensure you will get the perfect custom fit. Before you buy, I strongly recommend you go the the Jaybird REIGN site's FAQ pg for exact sizing info. http://www.jaybirdsport.com/static/img/reign/sizing-guide.jpg
Be aware, you want to determine the side-to-side width across the TOP of your wrist, not the circumference of your wrist. The REIGN is a 2 piece band. The fit/width of the top piece is what determines which size to buy. You then customize your fit with the bottom band, which is provided in 3 lengths.

SECURE: the magnetic locking mechanism ensures your band will never fall off. The design allows you to easily secure your band with one hand. Once it is magnetically secured, it will not come off until you manually disengage the magnets. Excellent design!

COMFORT: Due to the lightweight, smooth silicone band, this is the MOST comfortable activity wearable I have ever tried. As a tech professional, I am typing on my keyboard all day long and cannot wear any watch-type devices or jewelry on my wrists. This is the 1st tracker device I have found that I can wear all day, every day. I barely notice it's on my wrist. I wipe mine down with a damp cloth. I have had no irritation or discomfort. 5 stars!

TRACKING: The REIGN will track data by specific activity, which you will not get with other devices. It detects Walking, Swimming, Biking, Running and General activity. In addition to the 3 silicone magnetic wrist bands, they provide 2 stretch style athletic bands and an ankle biking band. The STEP tracking is accurate for me ( Compared my data for a couple of days with a FitBit and Treadmill)

SMART PHONE APP: The design of the SmartPhone app is a plus. The information provided is very good. In additional to your GoZone score, you are given 3 screens of data: Activity, Sleep and History. Each screen presents you with a Summary view and a Detail 'Timeline' view of that data.

VISUAL FEEDBACK: The band itself provides visual indication of your progress towards your GoZone Goal via lights. Each light represents 9% of your goal. (Dont bother enabling the 'Time' feature. The lights flash for 1 second and is pretty much useless)

CHARGING: Very easy to pop the device out of the band and charge on the charger that is included. Via USB cord, it can be charged thru your laptop or a plug, your choice. As stated, it takes about 3 hrs to initially charge. I pop mine onto the charger before I hop in the shower. Easy-peasy. Please note, if you lose the charger, you will have to buy a replacement since the charging doc is required.

USER GUIDE: I recommend you watch the online User Guide videos AND read thru the entire list of FAQs prior to purchasing/using the REIGN. There is a lot of info in the FAQs that is not covered in the User Guide videos that you will want to be aware of. A nice feature is, the videos are also part of the SmartPhone app.

HISTORY: the SmartPhone app. provides a History screen with Day, Week, Month & Year mode. Once you select your mode, you can then swipe thru by Day, Week, Month...... Very nice.

PERSONALIZED: The REIGN definitely does 'get to know you'. After the 1st week or so, the daily goal has adjusted, based on my history.

CONS:
GO ZONE: Upon waking up, you should be able to sync and log that day's GO ZONE feedback in 2 minutes. I have owned the REIGN for 11 days and rarely have I been ale to get GO ZONE to completed on the 1st try. Once the REIGN device is Connected to the SmartPhone app. and I Start Go Zone, I often get error messages and have to Start again. These issues are definitely specific to the GO ZONE feature, as I do not get errors throughout the day when syncing. This is the key feature of the device, so I expect it to work without issue and not have to battle with it.

SUPPORT: Unfortunately, I cannot give a good review on support. I sent a very detailed Email with screenshots from my SmartPhone listing the GoZone errors and Sleep monitoring issue I have experienced. The response I received was very friendly, however the only thing the reply told me was I could manually enter Sleep info in the app. There was no response to my detailed GoZone issues and questions.
SUPPORT Review Update 12-29-2015: I received another reply from Jaybird Support addressing my specific concerns and questions. They have provided me with instructions of how to reset my Reign pod, indicating this may resolve my specific issues.

READABILITY: I think the design of the app is great and it is easy to use. However, it is not so easy to read on your Smart Phone due to the funky color of the font (pale yellow-green) against a light grey background. It is not configurable. I understand these are the branded colors, but they do not lend themselves to readability on mobile devices.

DASHBOARD: There is not an online Dashboard. Your data is only available via your SmartPhone app. I went to the website and attempted to login assuming there would be an online dashboard. The online login is a separate account and is for purchases, only. The other tracker devices I have used have online Dashboards and settings, which I deem as a plus.

DATA SYNC: Data sync is on-demand, which preserves you SmartPhone battery (Yay!). However, for some reason, data for previous day(s) is not always shown in the app. Periodically, when you open the app on your phone, it will show all zero's after syncing. I have not been able to detect a pattern. It is an intermittent issue that cannot be reproduced, on demand. The work-a-round is to close and reopen the app.

TACTILE: Tapping the REIGN device 4 times does not active my lights. I have to rap it pretty hard, 8 to 12 times. I have mine set for progress feedback, only. The lights flash for 1 second. I would prefer a button that will allow me to quickly turn on the progress lights and turn them off when I release the button. ( If there were a manual button, the 'Time' feature may be of value).
text_fidelity_b: Jaybird Reign Advanced Active Fitness Recovery Band - Black - S/M

When I found it listed on Amazon with 240 reviews giving it an average rating of 4.8 stars, I followed my own advice to others and relied on the reviews written here. Normally I use an IWB, Belly Band, or pocket holster for concealed carry, but I also wanted to try an outside the waistband holster for a heavier weapon to see how it felt, how well it concealed (without printing or causing discomfort) and how easily it could be deployed.

So this was a new experience for me as I normally carry smaller and lighter firearms since we live in hot and humid Southwest Florida. I've never accidently displayed any weapon by mistake and have never been called out for "printing". I once even tried an experiment with my wife and had her guess what gun I was carrying and where I had it -- either in my cargo pants or tactical long-sleeved shirt. She guessed that I had a NAA .22 magnum in my right front pocket (Sticky Holster) only because she knew that I had carried one there for over 30 years. What she missed were the three.380's and three 9mm's that I had concealed in two ankle holsters, a Belly Band, another Sticky Holster, and two IWB's (appendix and 6 o'clock).

Now I'm breaking in this Relentless Tatical leather OWB holster which I can use in winter under jackets and in summer under untucked short-sleeved shirts. The holster is extremely well-made, is comfortable to wear, and fits my Defender perfectly. The price is on the money and there's just something about that new leather smell that still gets to me. Not many holsters have 240 reviews written about them. That alone says a lot about how the concealed carry market has recognized and put their stamp of approval on this piece of gear. Give it a fair trial, get used to it, and it it isn't your cup of tea just send it back within the 30 day trial window. I don't think that you'll be disappointed.

text_fidelity_a:
Empower Admittedly, it may seem too early for me to review the Empower Kettlebell & DVD I received yesterday. However, based on past workout purchases, and experiences, I believe this one's a keeper. I went for the 10-pound Kettlebell, and feel this is a good choice. It comes with a DVD with three levels of workouts, starting with one for beginners such as myself. It also includes warmup and cool-down routines, which are highly recommended before and after each workout respectively.

I started today, and after just one workout, I can already feel my core, leg, and arm muscles reacting to workout #1. While I have a little trouble with the 10-pound weight for some of the curl exercises, I modify the exercises to accommodate my lack of strength, and believe the 10-pound bell was a good choice because it allows me more room to grow -- which will be marked by my eliminating the need for modifications before moving on to the second workout.

In facing my 61st birthday, I'm active, and want to stay that way. This is why I'm determined to get in the best shape of my life (even in my early years, I've never been big on exercise). I started a month ago by purchasing a pair of Skecher Shape-ups, and taking brisk walks with my dogs each morning. To break the monotony, I purchased an MP3 player, and download books from the library. The time flies by!

I added resistance weeks ago with a trip to the gym, intent on going and working out every other day. Then reality hit. It took too long to get dressed, get my walk in, and then go to the gym, work out, come home and clean up. My mornings were shot. So I needed another way to achieve my goal.

A friend told me about Kettlebells. Now, after just one short Kettlebell workout, I've accomplished as much as when using several machines at the gym. The best part is it's fast. I can hop out of bed, and get it done quickly.

Based on numerous past workout experiences and money wasted on a variety of machines and other programs and gimmicks, I'm convinced this is what I've been searching for. I'd recommend it to anyone thinking of starting to get in shape, and wanting fast results. If you're new to working with weights, which I am not, you might want to start with the Empower 5-Pound KettleBell with DVD, and then work your way up to heavier Kettlebells. [[ASIN:B001O0EG7S Empower 10-Pound KettleBell with DVD]]

New Balance Step Counter Pedometer - Belt Clipon Pedometer Fitness Tracker Walking Meter with Removable Base Ideal for Women, Men, Kids to Count Steps, Distance, Calories Burned & Time, Black/Red This step counter doesn't count steps very accurately, and the buttons are easy to bump when unclipping the pedometer so that the step information is reset to zero and lost. There have been many times when testing the best way to use this when the steps showed zero when I checked it. In order to not over count steps due to random movement, the steps are not counted until you've done 10 similar steps in a row. Since I do a lot of work in the kitchen and gardening that is under 10 steps, then a pause, then more steps, this means a lot of steps are not being counted. Also, it seems like it is not counting those first 10 steps, either. If I step 50 steps in a row, it only counts like 32 steps. Frankly, an app on my phone works better than this. I had thought a dedicated device would work better, but I guess not. I will note that it seems to count steps better when this is clipped to my shoe rather than to my waistband. I'll update after little bit if I figure out how to make it work better.

The step counter comes with a battery, and you remove the plastic strip preventing connection in order to turn on the pedometer. It is then constantly on, though it does go into a sleep mode when there is no movement. The instructions that come with it are not very clear, but you're supposed to be able to set things like stride length. You hit the mode button to switch between steps, distance, calories burned, time spent walking, speed, the clock, and total steps. There is also a reset button along one edge and a set button along with other edge. You can remove the counter from the clip (mainly to access the battery chamber). My accidental reset problem has been when the buttons are near the top of the clip, where you have to squeeze to release the clip. I still seem to bump the buttons when the ends are switched, but it's not as often.

Problem is we needed a way to pull all the batteries out of the bike to even get close to the weight limit for the train crew to lift the bikes on the train.
